title: Independent reads and writes
summary: Use a fetcher when an operation should keep the current page and URL.

sections.title: Read a registered route
sections.body: load calls the target loader. Its result goes to fetcher.data and does not replace the page loader data or trigger page revalidation.

sections.title: Mutate a registered route
sections.body: Fetcher forms support POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE. Actions target registered routes, not arbitrary unregistered API URLs. A successful action revalidates the active page loader unless shouldRevalidate opts out.

sections.title: State and ownership
sections.body: A fetcher transitions idle → loading → idle for a read; idle → submitting → loading → idle for a successful mutation and revalidation. Each useFetcher instance owns independent data and cancellation. Its data persists during subsequent requests. Errors are exposed as fetcher.error.

sections.title: Navigation versus fetcher
sections.body: Form and Link navigate. fetcher.Form, fetcher.load, and fetcher.submit keep the URL, except when a handler returns a redirect. Existing fetchers are not globally cached or automatically refetched after another fetcher writes. Reload previews explicitly when needed.
